extracted.intended_audience: aircraft operators, maintenance personnel, repair stations, manufacturers, and interested members of the public (FAA commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for participating in FAA notice-and-comment rulemaking for proposed airworthiness directives (ADs), and the substantive compliance/inspection/repair requirements that would be mandated by those ADs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to participate / submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested persons are invited to participate in the making of the proposed rule by submitting such written data, views, or arguments as they may desire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should identify the regulatory docket number and be submitted in duplicate to the address specified above. All communications received on or before the closing date for comments specified above will be considered by the Administrator before taking action on the proposed rule. The proposals contained in this Notice may be changed in light of the comments received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topics on which comments are specifically invited
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are specifically invited on the overall regulatory, economic, environmental, and energy aspects of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should address any of these aspects in their written comments to assist FAA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment availability and public docketing
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments submitted will be available, both before and after the closing date for comments, in the Rules Docket for examination by interested persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A report summarizing each FAA/public contact concerned with the substance of the proposal will be filed in the Rules Docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of receipt procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters wishing the FAA to acknowledge receipt of their comments must submit a self-addressed, stamped post card on which the following statement is made: 'Comments to Docket Number [XX].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post card will be date/time stamped and returned to the commenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission format and identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications should identify the regulatory docket number and be submitted in duplicate to the address specified in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific docket/address given in the AD notice (examples in text: Northwest Mountain Region, Transport Airplane Directorate, ANM-103, Attention: Airworthiness Rules Docket No. XX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment deadline requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be received no later than the date specified in the notice (examples: February 20, 1990; February 24, 1990).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late comments may not be considered; use the deadline stated for the particular docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and examination of service information
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable service information may be obtained from the manufacturer (address given) and may be examined at the FAA regional office or the Standardization Branch/Seattle Aircraft Certification Office specified in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact details (manufacturer address and FAA office locations) are provided in each notice for obtaining or examining service documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory/economic/federalism certifications and docketed evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAA certifies whether the proposed regulation is a 'major rule' under Executive Order 12291, a 'significant rule' under DOT policies, and whether it will have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the Regulatory Flexibility Act; a copy of the draft evaluation is contained in the regulatory docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asserted as not significant, the notice still includes supporting estimates (number of affected U.S. airplanes, manhours per airplane, labor rate, total cost impact) and states federalism implications per Executive Order 12612.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability statement (models/parts/serial numbers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each AD includes an applicability clause identifying the affected airplane models, part numbers, and serial number ranges (e.g., 'Applies to all Model ATR42 series airplanes' or wheels with Loral P/N 5006858, 5006856-1, and 5006856-2, serial numbers OCT83-001 through OCT86-071).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance is required as indicated, unless previously accomplished; specific serial-number exclusions/notes may apply (see individual AD text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory inspection actions and methods (ATR42 visual/eddy-current inspections)
rubrics_metrics.description: For specified Loral wheel P/Ns and serial numbers: within 7 days or 100 landings after last inspection (whichever occurs later) perform a visual inspection of inboard wheel halves with airplane jacked to detect cracks in accordance with Loral Systems Group Service Bulletin ATR42-32-40-1, Revision 2; repeat at intervals not to exceed 7 days or 100 landings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a crack is detected, only one additional landing may be made after detection before the cracked inboard wheel half must be replaced. For another serial/part group, at each tire change perform an eddy current inspection or other nondestructive test per the service bulletin and replace any cracked inboard wheel half before further flight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption note for factory-built wheels (ATR42)
rubrics_metrics.description: MLG wheels with Loral Part Number 5006856-2, serial numbers OCT86-001 through OCT86-071 and NOV86-072 through AUG87-378, are factory built new wheels, and are not subject to the repetitive inspection requirements of the AD paragraphs A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check serial numbers against the AD note to determine inspection applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminating action via replacement (ATR42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement of inboard wheel halves with a new reinforced half wheel and replacement of the existing hub spacer with a modified hub spacer, in accordance with Aerospatiale Service Bulletin ATR42-32-0017 (or Revision 1), constitutes terminating action for the repetitive inspections required by paragraphs A and B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplishment per the referenced service bulletin ends repetitive-inspection obligations under the AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inspection thresholds by accumulated landings (A300 HFEC inspections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform a HFEC inspection of the horizontal stabilizer center box top integral skin in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A300-55-0038, with initial inspection timing dependent on airplane model and accumulated landings (detailed thresholds provided for Model A300 B2, A300 B4-100/B4-2C, and A300 B4-200 series airplanes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: A300 B2 — if <17,800 landings, initial before 19,800; if 17,800–22,800, within 2,000 landings; if ≥22,800, within 1,000 landings. See AD for model-specific thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat inspection intervals by model (A300)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no cracks are found, repeat the HFEC inspections at intervals specified by model: A300 B2 — intervals not to exceed 13,900 landings; A300 B4-100 and B4-2C — intervals not to exceed 12,400 landings; A300 B4-200 — intervals not to exceed 10,100 landings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the model-specific repeat-interval limits in paragraph B of the AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair requirement if cracks found (A300)
rubrics_metrics.description: If cracks are found in the HFEC inspections, repair prior to further flight in accordance with Airbus Service Bulletin A300-55-0038 and repeat inspections thereafter at the intervals specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repairs must follow the referenced service bulletin; inspections continue after repair as directed by the AD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options and compliance actions (Boeing 737 fuel feed tube)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prevent a fire hazard due to fuel tube chafing, accomplish one of the following within the compliance time: (1) Inspect the left engine fuel feed tube assembly for proper clearance and chafing in accordance with Boeing Service Bulletin 737-28-1055 Rev 1, adjust if inadequate, and replace any chafed tube per Boeing Service Bulletin 737-28-1084; or (2) Replace the left engine fuel feed tube in accordance with Boeing Service Bulletin 737-28-1084.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inadequate clearance or chafing is found, adjust or replace prior to further flight. Compliance was required within 3 months after the effective date of the AD in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification requirement to assure continuous indication (Boeing 737-400 APU EGT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify the APU instrumentation wiring in a manner that will assure continuous flight-compartment APU exhaust gas temperature (EGT) indication following an APU shutdown; the modification must be accomplished in a manner approved by the Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office, FAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance required within the next 1,000 hours time-in-service after the effective date of this AD unless previously accomplished; Boeing service bulletin may be referenced if approved prior to final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repair/replace prior to further flight requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the AD identifies a cracked or chafed part, the AD requires replacement or repair 'prior to further flight' (examples: replace cracked inboard wheel half before further flight; replace any chafed fuel tube prior to further flight; repair A300 cracks prior to further flight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions that are required 'prior to further flight' are immediate compliance items and must be accomplished before the airplane is next flown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate means of compliance (AMOC) approval and routing
rubrics_metrics.description: An alternate means of compliance or adjustment of the compliance time, which provides an acceptable level of safety, may be used when approved by the Manager, Standardization Branch, ANM-113, FAA, Northwest Mountain Region (or Manager, Seattle Aircraft Certification Office as specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request should be forwarded through an FAA Principal Maintenance Inspector (PMI), who will either concur or comment and then send it to the Manager (named office). Different ADs reference the appropriate Manager/office for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special flight permits to comply with AD
rubrics_metrics.description: Special flight permits may be issued in accordance with FAR 21.197 and 21.199 to operate airplanes to a base in order to comply with the requirements of the AD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FAR provisions when ferrying an aircraft to accomplish required work; follow applicable permit procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service documents distribution and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons affected by the directive who have not already received the appropriate service documents from the manufacturer may obtain copies upon request from the manufacturer; these documents may be examined at the FAA regional offices or the Standardization Branch/Seattle ACO specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manufacturer contact details and FAA office locations are provided; operators may request copies or visit FAA offices to examine documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-estimate reporting for affected operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed AD provides an estimate of the number of U.S.-registered airplanes affected, the estimated manhours per airplane to accomplish required actions, average labor cost per manhour, and total estimated cost impact on U.S. operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates support the FAA's certifications about economic impact and Regulatory Flexibility Act determinations.
